evals.name: find-expensive-feature-tool
evals.prompt: My Godot 4.7 village looks great now (warm sun with high-quality shadows, SDFGI, SSAO, SSIL, fog, MSAA 8x, 20k grass tufts) but it only runs ~50 fps on an RTX card. I want a tool to find out what is actually expensive, and a plan to get the fps back WITHOUT making it look noticeably worse. Write perf_bench.gd (GDScript I can drop in the scene) plus plan.md.
evals.expected_output: perf_bench.gd measures GPU time per configuration (viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu or equivalent) at a fixed view after warm-up, toggling features individually including leave-one-out; plan.md says vsync off for measurement, compare the same view, lower sub-settings (shadow max distance, shadow atlas size, soft shadow filter quality, MSAA samples, SDFGI half resolution/cascades, grass visibility range and no grass shadows) instead of removing the sun/features. Script compiles in Godot 4.7.

evals.name: should-i-disable-sun-shadows
evals.prompt: quick q: my godot 4.7 open village dropped to like 45 fps after I set up the DirectionalLight3D with nice soft shadows. should I just turn shadows off on the sun to get my fps back? answer in answer.md
evals.expected_output: Advises against removing the sun/its shadows outright; explains direction/colour vs shadow quality are separate; recommends directional_shadow_max_distance, shadow atlas size, soft shadow filter quality, PCSS/angular distance, split mode, grass/small props cast_shadow off; measure per feature at the same view with vsync off before deciding.
